final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is useful because it concedes the original overbroad certification theory was unsupported, but it does not cure the compliance defect. The policy text is explicit: rollout controls and monitoring can mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. On the available record, the affected loan modification support segment remains exposed, no reviewed risk acceptance is in evidence, and no implemented reviewed disclosure artifact is in evidence. A narrowed position of 'monitored, reversible launch with disclosure' may describe a more candid posture, but it still leaves the required compliance predicate unmet. This is therefore not merely compliant_with_caveats; the caveat identifies an unresolved condition required by policy.
remaining_concerns: The loan modification support segment remains below target and remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
No reviewed and approved risk acceptance is in evidence for the exposed loan modification support segment.
No admissible evidence shows the affected use case is excluded from rollout.
No admissible evidence shows the proposed model-card disclosure has been reviewed and implemented before launch.
The governing policy requires exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance; rollback, monitoring, and small-percentage rollout do not satisfy that predicate on their own.
